With this strategy, custom widgets that implement `getWidgetRenderState` will throw a TypeScript error. We still need to add a generic `getWidgetRenderState` independent of the `$$type`.

Generics were created to solve this specific problem. They're a solution to define an interface that we implement in our widgets, and that users can implement in their own widgets. Here we loose this API definition.

Why avoiding them?
That's a good point.

I'm not avoiding them, but was trying to compare them and I literally didn't know what's better and what has which drawbacks. I think https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/4518#discussion_r498073495 makes it enough to choose generics. Let me know if you have more thoughts on the drawbacks of this approach (discriminated type union)  in addition to that.
Yes, and I don't see why this is an issue :thinking:

IIUC, if a user is using TypeScript, and implement a custom widget with a $$type: let's say.. `ais.myCustomWidget`. Then the custom widget's type `Widget` won't include `getWidgetRenderState` and the user has no proper way to include it.

What I mean is that we can (must) add a generic `getWidgetRenderState` method to the base Widget type to avoid this and for the user to get proper typing in a custom widget.

Also users must not put a `$$type` key on a custom widget since this is for internal use only.

@francoischalifour I'm not sure what API definition we are loosing here. Also Generic have their own limitations and in our case we want to have stricter definition on our own widget than what we enforce for custom ones. This is where Generics find their limits here, forcing us to be less strict on our own widgets. I find discriminated type unions here to fit perfectly for what we want to accomplish while keeping the types more readable. For example here's what I have in mind: https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/311654f856a4b3625395a370e95ca606806efb6d/src/types/widget.ts#L237-L475

I think a generic for RenderState defaulting to any / an object / similar would make sense though, that way external users can still use very loose typescript if they want, but can also opt-in to the same safety as us. We won't be able to put custom widgets in uiState & render state without a separate generic on InstantSearch I guess

@yannickcr Can you help me understand, without generics, but with discriminated type unions, how to enable customers to create custom widgets and still let them implement `getWidgetRenderState` without type issue?

@eunjae-lee With discriminated type unions a custom widget created by the user will not have a `$$type` property, so it will match the `GenericWidget` type.

In that case if the user wants to implement `getWidgetRenderState` he will need to follow the type of `getWidgetRenderState` as implemented in `GenericWidget` (`getWidgetRenderState?: (renderOptions: InitOptions | RenderOptions) => any;` here but as @Haroenv said we could force it to return an object)
